examples.en: On weekends the school playground is open to the public.

examples.ko: 새 공원이 다음 달에 시민에게 개방될 거예요.
examples.en: The new park will be opened to the public next month.
The back door of this building was open only in the daytime.
In an open space, voices echo loudly.
I wish the park were open at night too.

examples.ko: 그 정원이 하루 동안 무료로 개방되었어요.
examples.en: The garden was opened free of charge for one day.

explain: '열리다'는 문이나 가게가 열리는 일상 말이고, '개방되다'는 건물, 시설, 시장처럼 많은 사람이나 다른 나라에 열려 있다는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '폐쇄되다'예요.
explain_en: 열리다 is the everyday word for doors and shops opening; 개방되다 suggests a building, facility, or market being open to many people or other countries. The opposite is 폐쇄되다.

examples.en: My passport gets renewed next month.
The contract was renewed automatically.
When the app is updated, new features appear.
Every time a record was broken, the crowd cheered.
The member information didn't update, so I made an inquiry.
Please check the updated price list.

explain: 유효 기간이 있는 것이 새로 이어지거나, 정보나 기록이 새것으로 바뀔 때 써요. 계약, 여권, 면허는 '연장'과 비슷하지만 새 기간으로 바꾸는 느낌이 강해요. 스포츠에서는 '기록이 갱신되다'가 기록을 깼다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요. 내가 직접 하면 '갱신하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when something with an expiry date is renewed, or information or a record is replaced with a new version. For contracts, passports and licenses it resembles 연장 (extension) but stresses a fresh term. In sports, 기록이 갱신되다 means a record was broken. When you do it yourself, use 갱신하다.

examples.ko: 민방위 훈련 날 경계경보 사이렌이 울렸어요.
examples.en: On the civil defense drill day, the alert siren sounded.

examples.ko: 갑자기 울린 경계경보 때문에 모두 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was startled by the alert that suddenly went off.

examples.ko: 경계경보 문자를 받고 가족에게 바로 전화했어요.
examples.en: I got an alert text and called my family right away.
The news reported that an alert had been issued.
I only felt relieved after the alert was lifted.
We had an alert evacuation drill at school.

explain: 적의 공습이 예상될 때 내리는 민방위 경보예요. 공습이 임박하면 '공습경보'가 되어 한 단계 더 급해요. 날씨 특보에는 '주의보'와 '경보'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the civil defense alert issued when an enemy air raid is expected. When a raid is imminent it becomes a '공습경보' (air-raid siren), one step more urgent. Weather advisories use '주의보' and '경보' instead.

examples.en: An event celebrating Liberation Day is held in the square.
The whole nation celebrated the Olympic gold medal.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 새 다리 개통을 경축하며 잔치를 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers held a feast celebrating the opening of the new bridge.

examples.ko: 나라의 큰 경사를 경축하기 위해 불꽃놀이를 했어요.
examples.en: They held fireworks to celebrate a great national occasion.

examples.ko: 학교 앞에 개교 백 주년을 경축한다는 현수막이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: A banner celebrating the school's 100th anniversary was hung in front of the school.
To celebrate the national holiday, every house flew the Taegukgi.

explain: 나라나 단체의 큰 경사를 크게 기뻐하며 축하할 때 써요. 친구 생일이나 합격 같은 개인적인 일에는 '축하하다'를 써요. '경축 행사'처럼 행사 이름에도 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when joyfully celebrating a big occasion for a nation or organization. For personal things like a friend's birthday or a passed exam, use '축하하다'. It also appears in event names such as '경축 행사'.

examples.en: The groundbreaking ceremony for the new hospital is held tomorrow.
The mayor also attended the apartment groundbreaking ceremony.

examples.ko: 기공식 날에는 비가 와서 행사가 조금 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: It rained on the day of the groundbreaking, so the event was a bit late.
I saw the bridge construction groundbreaking ceremony on the news.
I took a photo of them digging the first shovel at the groundbreaking.

examples.ko: 공장 기공식은 다음 달 초로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: The factory groundbreaking has been set for early next month.

explain: 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사이고, 반대로 공사가 끝났을 때 하는 행사는 '준공식'이에요. 비슷한 말로 '착공식'도 써요. 보통 '기공식을 열다/하다', '기공식에 참석하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: This is the event held when construction starts; the one held when it finishes is '준공식'. '착공식' is a similar word. People usually say '기공식을 열다/하다' or '기공식에 참석하다'.

examples.en: This app supports multiple languages, so it's convenient.
A multilingual notice is posted at the entrance.
Our company website was made in multiple languages.

examples.ko: 다국어 메뉴판 덕분에 외국인 손님도 편하게 주문해요.
examples.en: Thanks to the multilingual menu, foreign guests order easily.

examples.ko: 그 사전은 다국어 번역 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: That dictionary has a multilingual translation feature.
Multilingual announcements play at the airport.

explain: 여러 나라 말을 한꺼번에 쓰거나 지원할 때 써요. '다국어 지원', '다국어 안내'처럼 뒤에 다른 말과 붙어서 많이 나와요. 사람이 여러 언어를 할 때는 '여러 언어를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when many languages are used or supported at once. It often attaches to other words, as in '다국어 지원' and '다국어 안내'. For a person who speaks several languages, people say '여러 언어를 하다'.

examples.ko: 동절기에는 수도관이 얼지 않게 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: In winter, you have to be careful that the water pipes don't freeze.

examples.ko: 동절기 근무 시간이 한 시간 줄었어요.
examples.en: Winter working hours were cut by one hour.

examples.ko: 공사는 동절기를 피해서 봄에 시작할 거예요.
examples.en: The construction will start in spring, avoiding the winter season.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 동절기마다 운영 시간을 바꿔요.
examples.en: This library changes its opening hours every winter season.

examples.ko: 지금은 동절기라서 야외 수영장을 운영하지 않아요.
examples.en: It's the winter season now, so the outdoor pool isn't open.
This year is much colder than last winter season.

explain: '겨울'과 같은 시기를 말하지만 공지, 뉴스, 회사 규정처럼 공식적인 글에서 써요. 반대말은 '하절기'예요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '겨울'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It covers the same period as '겨울' but is used in official writing such as notices, news and company rules. The opposite is '하절기' (summer season). In daily conversation people just say '겨울'.

examples.en: I lost my child in the mall, so I went to the lost-child center.

examples.ko: 죄송한데 이 쇼핑몰에서 미아보호소는 어디에 있어요?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the lost-child center in this mall?

examples.ko: 직원이 길을 잃은 아이를 미아보호소로 데려갔어요.
examples.en: A staff member took the lost child to the lost-child center.

examples.ko: 아이가 울고 있어서 미아보호소에 먼저 연락했어요.
examples.en: The child was crying, so I contacted the lost-child center first.
There is a lost-child center next to the amusement park entrance.

examples.ko: 엄마를 찾을 때까지 아이는 미아보호소에서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The child waited at the lost-child center until finding his mom.

explain: '미아'는 길을 잃은 아이를 가리켜서 '미아가 되다', '미아를 찾다'처럼 같이 써요. 놀이공원이나 큰 쇼핑몰 같은 곳의 안내 표지에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: '미아' refers to a lost child, and it goes with phrases like '미아가 되다' and '미아를 찾다'. You often see this word on signs at amusement parks and large shopping malls.

en: getting in or out of a vehicle

examples.ko: 버스 승하차 때는 카드를 꼭 찍어야 해요.
examples.en: You must tap your card when getting on and off the bus.

examples.ko: 승하차하는 사람이 많아서 문 앞이 복잡해요.
examples.en: Many people are getting on and off, so it's crowded by the door.

examples.ko: 휠체어 승하차를 돕는 장치가 버스에 있어요.
examples.en: The bus has a device that helps wheelchairs get on and off.
Watch your step when boarding and getting off.
This stop has a lot of passengers getting on and off.
Please board or get off only after the train has fully stopped.

explain: '타고 내림'을 한 단어로 묶은 말이라 안내 방송, 안내문, 교통 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '타다'와 '내리다'를 따로 말해요. '승하차 인원', '승하차 시'처럼 명사로 써요.
explain_en: It packs 'getting on and off' into one word, so it appears in announcements, signs and transport news. In daily talk people say '타다' and '내리다' separately. It is used as a noun, as in '승하차 인원' and '승하차 시'.

examples.en: The wedding banquet hall is in the hotel basement.
The guests gathered in the banquet hall.
The banquet hall was full of music.

examples.ko: 연회장을 예약하려면 한 달 전에 연락하세요.
examples.en: To book a banquet hall, contact them a month in advance.
The year-end party is held in the banquet hall.
I'm looking for a hotel with a large banquet hall.

explain: 연회장은 피로연이나 송년회처럼 많은 사람이 모여 식사하는 큰 홀을 말해요. 결혼식을 올리는 곳은 '예식장'이라고 해서 연회장과 구분해요. 호텔에서는 '볼룸'이라고도 불러요.
explain_en: 연회장 is a large hall where many people gather to eat, such as for a wedding reception or a year-end party. The place where the wedding ceremony is held is called 예식장, which is different. Hotels sometimes call it a 볼룸.

en: announce in advance; give advance notice

examples.ko: 방송에서 다음 주 눈 소식을 예고했어요.
examples.en: The broadcast gave advance notice of snow next week.
The teacher announced the test in advance.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 새 이야기를 예고하며 끝나요.
examples.en: That movie ends by hinting at a new story.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 신곡 발표를 예고하고 있어요.
examples.en: This singer is teasing the release of a new song.

examples.ko: 한 달 전에는 꼭 예고해 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to give notice a month ahead.
As announced, prices go up from today.

explain: '알리다'와 달리 일이 일어나기 전에 미리 알릴 때 써요. 영화 예고편, '태풍 예고', '파업 예고'처럼 앞으로 있을 일에 써요. 예고 없이 일어난 일은 '예고 없이'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '알리다', it is used for letting people know before something happens, as in a movie trailer (예고편) or '태풍 예고'. It is for things still to come. Something that happens without warning is '예고 없이'.

examples.en: I bought snacks as comfort gifts to send to the soldiers.
The residents delivered comfort gifts to the elderly.

examples.ko: 상자 안 위문품에는 간식과 편지가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The comfort gifts in the box include snacks and a letter.
The children were happy when the comfort gifts arrived.

examples.ko: 위문품 구입비를 반 친구들이 함께 모았어요.
examples.en: My classmates pooled money together to buy the comfort gifts.

examples.ko: 위문품이라서 너무 비싼 건 안 샀어요.
examples.en: Since it was a comfort gift, I didn't buy anything too expensive.

explain: 그냥 '선물'과 달리 어려운 처지에 있는 사람을 위로하려고 보내는 물건이라는 점이 달라요. 병원, 복지시설, 재난 지역으로 보내는 물품 이야기에 잘 나와요. 병문안 갈 때 가져가는 것은 보통 '병문안 선물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike a plain '선물' (gift), it is something sent to comfort people in difficult situations. It comes up in talk about goods sent to hospitals, welfare facilities, or disaster areas. What you bring when visiting a sick person is usually called a '병문안 선물'.

examples.ko: 이 채소는 농약 잔류 검사를 통과했어요.
examples.en: This vegetable passed the pesticide residue test.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 이번 시즌에도 1부 리그 잔류가 목표예요.
examples.en: This team's goal this season is again to stay in the top league.

examples.ko: 토양에 잔류한 물질이 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Substances remaining in the soil can become a problem.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 고민 끝에 팀 잔류를 선택했어요.
examples.en: After much thought, the player chose to stay with the team.
The longer the stay, the more the cost increases.

examples.ko: 잔류 농약은 물로 씻으면 많이 줄어요.
examples.en: Residual pesticide is greatly reduced if you wash it with water.

explain: '남음'보다 딱딱해서 농약·약물처럼 남아 있는 성분이나, 팀·부대·리그에 계속 있는 것을 말할 때 써요. 반대로 떠나는 것은 '이탈'이나 '철수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than a plain word for 'leftover' and is used for remaining substances such as pesticides or drugs, and for staying on in a team, unit or league. Leaving is expressed with words like '이탈' or '철수'.

examples.ko: 아버지 회갑에는 가족끼리 식당에서 조촐하게 식사를 했어요.
examples.en: For my father's 60th birthday, the family had a modest meal at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 우리 결혼식은 조촐한 모임이었지만 정말 행복했어요.
examples.en: Our wedding was a small gathering, but we were really happy.

examples.ko: 생일 파티는 조촐해요. 케이크 하나에 친구 세 명이 전부예요.
examples.en: The birthday party is small. It's just one cake and three friends.
The table was simple, but it was full of care.
My home is so modest that I'm embarrassed to invite guests.

examples.ko: 퇴직 기념 모임은 조촐히 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold the retirement party in a small, simple way.

explain: 작고 소박하지만 깔끔하고 정돈된 느낌이에요. 모임, 상차림, 집에 많이 쓰고, '초라하다'와 달리 부정적인 느낌이 없어요. 영어 'cozy'보다는 'modest and neat'에 가까워요.
explain_en: It has a feel of being small and simple but tidy and neat. It is often used for gatherings, meals and homes, and unlike '초라하다' (shabby) it is not negative. It is closer to 'modest and neat' than to 'cozy'.
